Keira Knightley plays aspiring author Colette as a passionate and fiercely independent figure. She is looking to establish an ar- tistic identity of her own at a time when patriarchal wisdom has it that “lady writers don’t sell”. First seen as a 19-year-old in 1892, she is a young woman without a dowry or any obvious prospects. Colette may seem demure but that doesn’t stop her from hav- ing sex in the barn with the much older Henry Gauthier-Villars (known as “Willy”), a city slicker who served in the army with her father.
